key_insight: Medical image representations converge only modestly, and this shared geometry is driven more by self-supervised pretraining than by clinical supervision or model scale.
clinical_relevance: A classifier can transfer across encoders and even to unseen hospitals with about 85% of within-encoder performance, suggesting interoperability is possible but must be validated carefully.
method: Compared 18 image and 7 text encoders across 5 imaging modalities.
Controlled for data, architecture, and scale while varying only the training objective.
Evaluated representational similarity and transfer, including a synthetic model check.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 650,982 chest radiographs from six datasets and found matched self-supervised encoders aligned most on chest radiography (40.4%), versus label-supervised (21.1%) and image-text (3.3%).
watch_item: The convergence does not extend well to clinical language or radiologist-defined similarity, so shared representations may be weakest in subgroup-specific or judgment-based use cases.
paper_title: Self-supervision drives representational convergence in medical foundation models more than clinical supervision
